source: Not a page export. On 18 Oct 2026 Saqlain chose to accept the recommended picks in bulk. Claude first re-read the 20 close calls and weak matches and the controls left with no criteria. The rows below are Claude's corrected picks; every other proposed row is accepted as proposed (apply_rekey_decisions.py --accept-remaining).

NIST.ID.AM.07.TC3.note: Claude's corrected pick: the criterion tests the classification scheme and labels, which is AST-04, not the inventory.

NIST.ID.AM.08.TC3.note: Claude's corrected pick: disposal and sanitization records are AST-12's test.

NIST.ID.IM.03.TC3.note: Claude's corrected pick: updating a policy from a lesson learned is atom b, which maps to GOV-19.

CH2.SECURITY.1.TC3.note: Claude's corrected pick: backups are RES-04; the word match failed because every atom of this record is generic.

CH3.CORRECT.2.TC3.note: Claude's corrected pick: passing erasure on to processors is part of erasure on request, not the request channel.

CB.TRANSFER.2.TC2.note: Claude's corrected pick: government transfer orders are tracked under PSC-05, matching CB.TRANSFER.1.TC3.

CB.TRANSFER.1.TC1.note: Claude's corrected pick: the cross-border flow inventory is PSC-06's own test (atom b maps there as equal and full).

CB.TRANSFER.1.TC4.note: Claude's corrected pick: reconciling hosting regions with the inventory is in PSC-06's statement.

NIST.GV.PO.01.TC5.note: Tests two controls: violations (RSK-10) and exceptions (RSK-42). Kept on RSK-10 because a criterion attaches to one control.
